thesisQuality.basis: Strong current adoption and breadth with raised outlook, but durable moat/value capture is moderated by interoperability and acquisition integration uncertainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q3 sales, underlying orders, operating cash flow and free cash flow all grew and outlook was raised; non-recurring tariff-refund and adjusted-vs-GAAP effects keep the assessment below exceptional.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September 2026 market capitalization near $83.6B and trailing P/E around 34.4x indicate a demanding valuation relative to the presently evidenced growth profile; upside is plausible but asymmetry is not demonstrated.

catalystScore.basis: Raised 2026 outlook, grid deployments and ongoing industrial-AI/test expansion provide identifiable catalysts, but timing and incremental economics of acquisitions remain uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Current execution and disclosure are adequate-to-strong, but acquisition-led portfolio transformation leaves material capital-allocation and integration uncertainty.

alignment2036.basis: Automation, grid management, industrial software and test capabilities directly address durable power, industrial productivity, reliability and infrastructure needs across plausible long-duration futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Sensing/control, software, test/measurement and grid capabilities provide multiple demand engines with reusable industrial-domain capability, though portfolio breadth also raises integration complexity.

bottleneckControl.basis: Emerson participates meaningfully in automation and grid constraints, but evidence does not establish an irreplaceable monopoly bottleneck and customers retain heterogeneous stack options.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Exposure spans power, industrial automation, software and test markets, providing several demand paths; geographic/end-market variability and acquisition execution remain meaningful concentration risks.

substitutionResilience.basis: Domain integration and installed industrial capability create moderate replacement barriers, but interoperable competing automation/software stacks remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Current evidence supports broad operations but does not demonstrate exceptional multi-source redundancy; tariff and geopolitical exposure remain explicit operating risks, so confidence is capped in the mixed band.

pricingPower.basis: The 10-Q attributes underlying growth partly to 3% higher price, demonstrating current price realization, but durable pricing power independent of mix/inflation recovery is not established.

riskEvidence.basis: Material but non-terminal risks include adjusted-vs-GAAP profitability quality, acquisition integration/capital allocation, demanding valuation, substitution, tariffs and geopolitical variability.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability and recent operating claims have exact primary lineage with duplicate origins collapsed; current independent market data closes valuation context, while some moat, supply-chain and pricing-power facts remain undisclosed or issuer-dominant.

scoreRecord.thesis: Emerson combines industrial automation, software, grid and test capabilities that benefit from durable infrastructure digitization and power-system complexity; current execution is strong, but valuation and acquisition/integration economics constrain upside asymmetry.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A demanding valuation plus acquisition-led integration, adjusted-profit quality and credible interoperable substitutes could compress returns even if end-market demand remains healthy.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Delivery against raised fiscal-2026 outlook and evidence that grid/industrial-AI/test investments convert into durable organic growth and cash economics.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the methodology-weighted component base. Risk and confidence are preserved separately for downstream locked gate/penalty treatment; this artifact does not mutate canonical score state.
